title: Choose the page structure
question: The world stays fixed: white→red flood, pepper canvases, the giant wordmark. Pick how the full studio page is composed around it.

options.label: The pepper is the camera
options.thesis: One hero pepper canvas pins and travels the whole page, and each section is a set it moves through.
options.viewport: Original hero: the wordmark across the bottom and intro copy top-left. After the flood, the pepper swarm detaches one pepper that rides into section two.
options.risk: The travelling pepper has to be choreographed per breakpoint, and on mobile it shrinks to a corner companion.

options.label: Wordmark as architecture
options.thesis: THIRTY / SIX / STUDIOS split into three acts. Each word is a section's giant structural masthead, with canvases masked inside the letters.
options.viewport: Original hero unchanged. Scrolling splits the wordmark: 'Thirty' anchors the studio intro, 'Six' the services and process, 'Studios' the work and contact.
options.risk: The type does a lot of work, so section copy has to stay disciplined or the page turns into a type specimen.

options.label: Two-sided page
options.thesis: The flood becomes a site-wide mode: white is the studio talking, red is the studio playing, and every section has both faces.
options.viewport: Original hero. The flood control stays reachable in the header, so any section can be flipped to its red, canvas-alive face.
options.risk: Two versions of every section doubles the content work, and the red face has to give more than a colour swap.
